episode_title: Nicole Armstrong QED-C #DESIGNtoCHANGE PODcast Year+5 with Ruud Janssen recorded live in Washington DC Arlington 7 Oct 2026

real_qa.q: What strategy did the Quantum Economic Development Consortium implement to align events with organizational goals?
real_qa.r: Nicole Armstrong halted most of the existing events at QEDC upon arrival, determining they were not strategically sound. She then established a two-cycle flagship event strategy: a spring event focused on the global quantum industry report to provide data-driven industry understanding, and a fall conference in November addressing a coordination agenda to identify industry gaps and collaboration needs between government, industry, and academia.
real_qa.requete: Quantum Economic Development Consortium event strategy

real_qa.q: How does augmented event design differ from traditional analog event design in execution speed and stakeholder engagement?
real_qa.r: Augmented event design produces higher quality outputs much faster, but requires designers to slow down their own thinking to digest the robust documents before engaging leadership. The analog model features critical stakeholder participation throughout the design process, while augmented design can move forward with fewer collaborators involved, risking stakeholder buy-in and requiring designers to become 'journey makers' to bring leaders along the entire thinking process.
real_qa.requete: augmented event design vs analog event design

real_qa.q: What was the attendance and satisfaction outcome of the Quantum Economic Development Consortium's first flagship event in April 2026?
real_qa.r: The first QEDC flagship event achieved over 90 percent attendance ratio and off-the-charts NPS scores, with attendees responding positively to the innovative program aspects. Armstrong noted this validated the design process, as the event performed exactly as strategically designed.
real_qa.requete: QEDC April 2026 flagship event results attendance NPS

real_qa.q: What organizational changes did Nicole Armstrong implement at QEDC within the first year?
real_qa.r: Armstrong reduced the event calendar from three to four annual plenary meetings down to two flagship meetings, shifted from free to paid events, changed membership from members-only to open access, and maintained sponsorship efforts. She fundamentally repositioned how the organization uses events to deliver strategic value rather than operating them as routine activities.
real_qa.requete: QEDC event calendar changes plenary meetings flagship

real_qa.q: Why is the event design process considered an underrated skill for event managers to talk leadership out of unnecessary events?
real_qa.r: Armstrong argues that an event manager's ability to articulate strategic value, help clarify desired outcomes, and communicate why events are not the appropriate approach demonstrates clear understanding of business objectives. This positions the professional in leadership's eyes differently, showing strategic thinking rather than just tactical execution.
real_qa.requete: event manager strategic value business objectives

real_qa.q: What challenge does augmented event design create when organizational strategy is not clearly defined?
real_qa.r: Augmented event design has no strategic lid and will push organizational thinking upward into company-wide strategy and industry-level change without gatekeeping. If the organization lacks proper gates on portfolio, mandate, or operational capacity, the event design escalates beyond traditional event owner scope into organizational strategy creation and industry positioning.
real_qa.requete: augmented event design organizational strategy limitations

guest.bio_context: Nicole Armstrong was part of Cohort 1 of the Event Design Certificate Program in San Diego in 2015. She has worked on strategic event design across multiple organizations including the Internet Society, MicroStrategy, and MITRE in the Washington D.C. area. She started at QEDC just under a year ago, shortly before Halloween, and has led significant organizational transformation through event strategy and design.
